chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, saying: He narrated to us Nasr ibn Mizahim al-Manqari, from Abu Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him)

He said: I have ten [characteristics] from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) which no one before me was given, and no one after me will be given. He said to me: O Ali, you are my brother in this world and the Hereafter. You are the closest of people to me in standing [before God] on the Day of Resurrection. My dwelling and your dwelling in Paradise are facing each other, like the dwellings of two brothers. You are the Trustee, you are the Guardian, you are the Vizier. Your enemy is my enemy, and my enemy is the enemy of God. Your friend is my friend, and my friend is the friend of God.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics of Ali from the Prophet mentioned in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith serves as a foundational text for the doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation), emphasizing Ali’s unique spiritual and political authority as the Prophet’s *Wasi* (successor) and *Wali* (guardian). The description of their dwellings in Paradise facing each other underscores the inseparable bond between Prophethood and Imamate, while the alignment of their enemies with God’s enmity highlights the theological stakes of accepting or rejecting Ali’s leadership.
